questions.question: Which artery supplies the breast through perforating branches that pierce the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th intercostal spaces?
questions.explanation: The internal thoracic (mammary) artery supplies the breast via its perforating branches in the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th intercostal spaces.

questions.question: Which branches of the axillary artery supply the breast?
questions.explanation: The axillary artery supplies the breast through its lateral thoracic, superior thoracic, and acromiothoracic branches.

questions.question: The posterior intercostal arteries supply the breast through which branches?
questions.explanation: The posterior intercostal arteries supply the breast through their lateral branches.

questions.question: Which of the following is a vein that drains the breast?
questions.explanation: The venous drainage of the breast takes place by the axillary, internal thoracic, and posterior intercostal veins.

questions.question: Before running into superficial and deep sets, the veins of the breast converge to form what?
questions.explanation: The veins converge towards the base of the nipple where they form an anastomotic venous circle.

questions.question: The superficial veins of the breast drain into which vein?
questions.explanation: The superficial veins drain into the internal thoracic vein.

questions.question: Through which venous route can breast cancer metastasize to the brain?
questions.explanation: Cancer cells can travel through posterior intercostal veins to the vertebral venous plexus and then to the brain.

questions.question: The nerve supply of the breast is derived from which intercostal nerves?
questions.explanation: The nerve supply is derived from the 2nd to 6th intercostal nerves through their anterior and lateral cutaneous branches.

questions.question: The sensory nerve endings in the nipple and areola stimulate the release of milk in response to what?
questions.explanation: The sensory nerve endings stimulate the release of milk from the mammary gland in response to suckling by the infant.

questions.question: Which hormone controls the secretion of milk from the breast?
questions.explanation: The secretion of milk from the breast is not under neural control but by prolactin hormone secreted by the pituitary gland.

questions.question: Which group of lymph nodes lies along the internal thoracic vessels?
questions.explanation: Internal mammary nodes lie along the internal thoracic vessels.

questions.question: Which lymph nodes lie in the deltopectoral groove?
questions.explanation: Cephalic (deltopectoral) nodes lie in the deltopectoral groove.

questions.question: The lymphatics draining the breast are divided into which two groups?
questions.explanation: The lymphatics draining the breast are divided into superficial and deep groups.

questions.question: A plexus of lymph vessels deep to the areola is called what?
questions.explanation: A plexus of lymph vessels deep to the areola is called the subareolar plexus of Sappey.

questions.question: The superficial lymphatics of the breast of one side communicate with those of which side?
questions.explanation: The superficial lymphatics of the breast of one side communicate with those of the opposite side.

questions.question: Into which group of nodes is lymph from the lateral quadrants of the breast drained?
questions.explanation: The lymph from the lateral quadrants is drained into the anterior axillary or pectoral group of lymph nodes.

questions.question: Lymph from the medial quadrants is drained into which nodes?
questions.explanation: The lymph from the medial quadrants is drained into internal mammary lymph nodes.

questions.question: What percentage of lymph from the breast is drained into the axillary nodes?
questions.explanation: About 75% of the lymph from the breast is drained into axillary nodes.

questions.question: What percentage of lymph from the breast is drained into internal mammary lymph nodes?
questions.explanation: About 20% of the lymph from the breast is drained into internal mammary lymph nodes.

questions.question: What percentage of lymph from the breast is drained into posterior intercostal lymph nodes?
questions.explanation: About 5% of the lymph from the breast is drained into the posterior intercostal lymph nodes.

questions.question: Breast cancer arises from the epithelial cells of which structure?
questions.explanation: Breast cancer arises from the epithelial cells of the lactiferous ducts.

questions.question: In which quadrant does breast cancer occur in about 60% of cases?
questions.explanation: In about 60% of cases, breast cancer occurs in the upper lateral quadrant.

questions.question: What clinical sign refers to the skin appearance similar to an orange peel due to obstruction of superficial lymphatics?
questions.explanation: Peau d'orange appearance is due to obstruction of superficial lymphatics.

questions.question: Infiltration of lactiferous ducts by cancer cells can lead to what clinical sign?
questions.explanation: Retraction of the nipple is due to infiltration and fibrosis of lactiferous ducts.

questions.question: What is the name of the secondary tumor in the ovary caused by the spread of breast cancer cells?
questions.explanation: Cancer cells can migrate transcoelomically and deposit on the ovary producing a secondary tumor called Krukenberg's tumor.

questions.question: How many steps are there in breast self-examination?
questions.explanation: The text outlines six steps of breast self-examination.

questions.question: During breast self-examination, when should steps 4 and 5 be repeated?
questions.explanation: Steps 4 and 5 should be repeated in a lying down position as the breasts are flattened, making them easier to palpate.

questions.question: The breast develops from an ectodermal thickening called what?
questions.explanation: The breast develops from an ectodermal thickening called the milk line or ridge of Schultz.

questions.question: Where does the milk line extend from and to?
questions.explanation: The milk line extends from the axilla to the groin.

questions.question: In the pectoral region, the thickened ectodermal structure gives off how many solid cords?
questions.explanation: It gives off 15-20 solid cords that grow in the underlying mesenchyme.

questions.question: The stroma of the breast develops from which germ layer?
questions.explanation: The stroma of the breast develops from surrounding mesoderm.

questions.question: Supernumerary nipples appearing along the milk ridge are known as what?
questions.explanation: Polythelia refers to supernumerary nipples which appear along the milk ridge.

questions.question: If the nipple fails to develop from the ectodermal pit, what condition occurs?
questions.explanation: Retracted or inverted nipple occurs if the nipple fails to develop from the ectodermal pit.

questions.question: The development of more than one breast along the milk line is called what?
questions.explanation: Polymastia refers to the development of more than one breast along the milk line.

questions.question: Development of breasts in males mainly at puberty is known as what?
questions.explanation: Gynecomastia is the development of breast in males, mainly at puberty.

questions.question: Gynecomastia is usually thought to occur due to what?
questions.explanation: It is usually bilateral and thought to occur due to hormonal imbalance.

questions.question: Which structure is considered the most important surface feature of the pectoral region in the female?
questions.explanation: The breast is the most important structure of the pectoral region in females.

questions.question: What is the largest muscle of the pectoral region?
questions.explanation: Pectoralis major is the largest muscle of the pectoral region.

questions.question: Which muscle is considered the key muscle of the axilla?
questions.explanation: The pectoralis minor is considered the key muscle of the axilla because it divides the axillary artery into three parts.

questions.question: Where do most of the lymph vessels of the upper limb drain into?
questions.explanation: Most of the superficial lymph vessels of the upper limb drain into the lateral group of axillary lymph nodes.

questions.question: What does the subareolar plexus of Sappey refer to?
questions.explanation: It is a plexus of lymph vessels deep to the areola that drain into the anterior axillary lymph nodes.

questions.question: What are the interpectoral lymph nodes also known as?
questions.explanation: Interpectoral lymph nodes are also known as Rotter's lymph nodes.

questions.question: What is the most common site of breast cancer?
questions.explanation: The most common site of breast cancer is the upper and outer quadrant of the breast.

questions.question: Which muscle forms the anterior wall of the axilla along with the clavipectoral fascia?
questions.explanation: Pectoralis major, subclavius, and pectoralis minor form the anterior wall of the axilla.

questions.question: Which structure forms the medial boundary of the cervico-axillary canal?
questions.explanation: The outer border of the first rib forms the medial boundary of the cervico-axillary canal.

questions.question: Which nerve is also known as the nerve to serratus anterior?
questions.explanation: The long thoracic nerve is also called the nerve to serratus anterior.

questions.question: Which structure is located immediately inferior to the inferior angle of the scapula?
questions.explanation: The eighth rib is palpable immediately inferior to the inferior angle of the scapula.

questions.question: The triangle of auscultation is bounded by the latissimus dorsi, the medial border of the scapula, and which muscle?
questions.explanation: The boundaries are the trapezius, latissimus dorsi, and the medial border of the scapula.

questions.question: What is the commonest cause of lymphedema of the upper limb?
options: Removal of axillary lymph nodes during mastectomy
questions.explanation: Removal of axillary lymph nodes during mastectomy commonly causes lymphedema of the upper limb.

questions.question: Which muscle is responsible for the rounded contour of the shoulder?
questions.explanation: The deltoid forms the rounded contour of the shoulder.
